analysis.title: GS Basics - Scarcity vs Returns. Defense. US Fundamental Cut.
key_insights: Positioning saw extraordinary de-risking last week, especially in US long/short TMT. It was the largest cut in gross exposure since Covid and the biggest cut in net since Liberation day. Almost everything linked to AI spending was sold.

The post mid-term rally lasted 24 hours. Short covering was followed by the view that one cannot be this pessimistic on AI spending and this optimistic on the broader economy. The SPX moved outside its recent range, gamma support disappeared and CTA selling accelerated.

Last week had more than 11mm puts trade in a single day, the largest put volume day on record, above the prior high in Apr '25. Index puts led, and single-stock put activity was the 4th highest day ever.
Models suggest another ~$25bn+ of potential CTA supply in SPX this week.

Asia saw a partial semis rebound that faded through the session: TSMC +4.6%, MediaTek +9.8%, Tokyo Electron +2.7%, Advantest +1.29%, Taiex +4.9%, Nikkei +2.3%, Kospi -80bps. Taiwan's tighter short selling rules and NT$500bn stabilization fund are providing support.

NDX futures would probably be higher without the weekend Nvidia/Jensen Huang headlines. The author reads these as idiosyncratic rather than a broader AI read-through, but they could affect sentiment. CoreWeave (Tuesday) and Nebius (Thursday) matter more for underlying AI sentiment.

Oil is lower to start the week with no weekend escalation in Iran. Trump suggested further strikes are unlikely if negotiations progress, while Rubio said talks have been largely unproductive. The author expects the escalation premium to return to oil by Wednesday/Thursday absent diplomatic progress.

Russia/Ukraine: trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, with prediction markets at 10-15% odds of a year-end ceasefire. The author's base case is a prolonged conflict, and he highlights the extraordinary derating in defense.

US defense spending could be maintained at the top line in a lame duck compromise with Democrats on healthcare. European defense has seen multiple compression from ceasefire headlines and EU fiscal debates, but NATO 2%+ GDP commitments and multi-year order backlogs mean a lot of bad news is priced in.

On AI, the author does not accept the long-term bear case that power constraints, permits and political delays undermine the buildout. If demand is real, capacity will move to other states, countries or alternative power sources. He cites Mississippi, xAI's 2GW Southaven buildout and over $25 billion in AWS commitments.

Oversupply, not power or permitting, is called the key medium-term risk. GPU spot rental rates remain supported by scarcity, but optimization and smaller specialized models are compressing per-token inference costs. The bear argument is that efficiency gains could outpace demand growth.
Semis look oversold. The author would move up the quality curve first (ASML, TSMC). Whether to buy or sell the Friday bounce depends on evidence on demand and monetization.

The macro backdrop improved: energy lower, rates retracing and credit spreads tightening. Nasdaq broke below its 200-day average, while the S&P's broader trend remains intact. CTA supply and retail selling are headwinds, with CPI the immediate catalyst. The best outcome is range-bound trading so implied volatility compresses and systematic demand rebuilds.

This week: Congress returns for the lame duck session, with a bipartisan energy permitting bill possibly positive for data centers but uncertain. Treasury auctions are 3yr Monday, 10yr Tuesday and 30yr Thursday. CPI on Tuesday is the main macro event. Friday's payrolls were +165k, wages +0.4% MoM and unemployment 4.1%.
